#1974. Jose Mourinho sends clear Real Madrid message to Eder Militao and Antonio Rudiger after PSV double substitution

By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 19:56

Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has offered a revealing assessment of his defensive hierarchy after substituting Eder Militao and Antonio Rudiger at half-time during Tuesday's 5-1 Champions League victory over PSV Eindhoven.

Los Blancos were trailing 1-0 at the Santiago Bernabeu when Mourinho made three changes at the interval, withdrawing both experienced centre-backs alongside Aurelien Tchouameni. Ibrahima Konate and Dean Huijsen entered in defence, while Jude Bellingham replaced the French midfielder.

The decision preceded a remarkable turnaround. Madrid scored five unanswered goals in the second half, with Bellingham, Federico Valverde, Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Junior contributing to a victory that maintained their perfect Champions League record after five matches.

Although Mourinho insisted that the improvement was primarily down to a collective change in mentality, his explanation for replacing Militao and Rudiger offered an insight into why Konate and Huijsen have established themselves as his preferred central-defensive partnership.

The Portuguese coach acknowledged that the two younger defenders currently benefit from greater match sharpness, while identifying specific qualities that make them particularly valuable to his system.

Speaking to Movistar after the match, Mourinho explained that his decision had been influenced by several factors, including the yellow cards shown to Rudiger and Tchouameni during the opening period.

"A bit of everything," he said when asked whether the substitutions were motivated by fitness, disciplinary concerns or a desire to change the game.

"We had two players on yellow cards in a game against some very quick players, which was a risk."

However, Mourinho's subsequent assessment was arguably more significant for the two defenders who had been withdrawn.

"Obviously, the two centre-backs who have been playing more regularly are in a better rhythm," he continued.

"Dean is our best player at bringing the ball out from the back, Konate is playing pretty well... and I thought those changes could help us."

Those comments underline the advantages currently enjoyed by Huijsen and Konate, who have become Mourinho's regular pairing since the beginning of the campaign.

Huijsen's ability to progress possession from defence is particularly important in a Madrid side expected to dominate the ball, while Konate provides the physical presence and defensive intensity required when the team presses high.

Both qualities were evident in the second half against PSV, when Madrid pushed their defensive line forward and prevented the Dutch visitors from progressing comfortably through midfield.

Mourinho nevertheless resisted the suggestion that his defensive substitutions alone had transformed the contest.

The former Chelsea and Manchester United manager also credited Bellingham's introduction and a collective improvement in pressing, explaining that his players had struggled to win individual battles before the interval.

"The second half was a question of mentality," Mourinho said. "We made changes, yes, and Jude is a different kind of player who gives us what we lacked in the first half, but collectively we were better in the second half."

His explanation makes it difficult to interpret the removal of Militao and Rudiger as an outright rejection of either player. Yet publicly highlighting the superior rhythm and individual qualities of their competitors offers a clear indication of the current pecking order.

The situation is particularly delicate for Rudiger, whose contract expires in June 2027.

The 33-year-old German has found regular opportunities difficult to secure under Mourinho, and reports in Spain have suggested that Real Madrid are increasingly unlikely to offer him another extension.

His experience remains an asset, particularly across a demanding season involving several competitions, but his reduced role raises questions about whether he will remain at the Bernabeu beyond next summer.

The Brazil international remains under contract until June 2028, although his recent career has been disrupted by two serious anterior cruciate ligament injuries and further muscular problems.

He has played only five minutes in La Liga this season, with his Champions League appearances providing most of his opportunities to regain competitive sharpness.

Tuesday's meeting with PSV represented another chance to demonstrate his readiness for a more prominent role. Instead, his involvement ended after 45 minutes as Mourinho turned to the partnership that has largely carried Madrid's defence this season.

The Brazilian's limited playing time makes the manager's comments about rhythm particularly relevant. Regaining his previous level requires regular appearances, but those opportunities are difficult to obtain while Konate and Huijsen continue to perform.

Huijsen's emergence has already complicated Militao's attempts to recover a starting place, with the Spain international establishing himself as a central figure in Mourinho's defensive plans.

Konate, meanwhile, has made a strong impression following his arrival from Liverpool, offering the combination of athleticism and defensive aggression that the Portuguese coach values.

The two established internationals therefore face different uncertainties. Rudiger must consider his future as his contract approaches its conclusion, while Militao has more time remaining on his deal but needs to demonstrate that he can compete consistently for a starting position.

Mourinho has not announced plans to sell either defender, and Tuesday's substitutions should not be regarded as confirmation of their departures.

However, the manager's unusually explicit assessment of his centre-backs has reinforced the challenge facing both players: Konate and Huijsen currently possess the match rhythm, tactical qualities and established partnership that make them difficult to displace.

#1973. Scott Parker damns his own players with this painful one-word home truth | West Ham News

Scott Parker could do little else other than state the obvious last night as West Ham plumbed new depths of mediocrity against their south coast opponents. For the first time this season, the league’s top scorers failed to find their opponent’s net despite again hitting the woodwork twice.

Speaking after the game, Parker came up with a new expression for ‘pulling their finger out’ – when speaking to West Ham tv:

“We need to fix up as a group and as a team and give ourselves a platform.”

This is an honest group. They’re probably too desperate, really and I think that’s weighing quite heavy and you can see that.

it’s just certain moments we’re a little bit soft in certain moments. We’re easy to play against in certain moments.”

Which means, as we can all see for ourselves it is less about the quality of the play, more about the mental resilience of the eleven on the pitch who have seemingly lost – for the time being – the ability to take another low blow and fight back. Conceding one goal away at Portsmouth is no disaster. Failing to register two goals against them is the real failing.

Another year, another hit: Soucek’s commitment to this team stands head, shoulders, torso and boots above some within the limp lettuce line up. Right now it ss more about the character of those selected than the ability.

At times earlier in the season West Ham would have romped down the other end and banged in three in quick succession to redress the balance and grab the points. And that is what Parker needs to find again. It isn’t the magic fix of a ‘perfect’ defensive performance, our players aren’t good enough to give us that. It is a mental resilience that ten didn’t have last night.

Eleven Tomas Souceks, players who are prepared to bleed for this club, will do nicely.

#1972. Viktor Gyökeres’ Sweden resurgence raises Arsenal questions, but the January exit is far from certain

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Viktor Gyökeres is reminding Arsenal of his prolific goal scoring capabilities.

The striker found the back of the net twice in Sweden’s 3-2 Nations League win against Bosnia and Herzegovina on November 14, both times from the spot to take his total to four in the Nations League this season.

The win also means they have booked their place in League A with one match left to play in the group, and Gyökeres has certainly played his part in this excellent run.

However, the performance will raise questions about his future at the club. The idea that he may be leaving in January is a possibility that needs to be looked at.

There is a stark difference between his international and club form.

Gyökeres has only played 181 minutes in seven Premier League games this season, starting just once as Kai Havertz has usually been preferred in central areas.

However, he has had more opportunities to play in European competition. Gyökeres has started three of Arsenal’s four matches in the Champions League, scoring one goal and providing two assists.

Gyökeres is not totally out of Arteta’s plans, but he will not play much domestically.

He has been in fine form internationally recently. Sweden are building their attack around his movement and penalty area presence, meaning he will have chances to regularly perform.

However, just because he is doing well internationally does not mean he will start regularly for the club. Arteta has other attacking options and tactics to consider.

There have been suggestions surrounding Gyökeres’ future, with reports that Arsenal may look to add more attacking flair to their squad.

AC Milan and Juventus have also been linked, but there is no agreement or suggestion that either club is looking to make a January move for the forward.

Gyökeres has opened up about the speculation.

In an interview with Swedish media outlet Fotbollskanalen during the international break, he stated that he would like to stay at the club. The player also denied any issues with his relationship with Arteta, stating that they have good communication.

However, the player may not stay forever, as he has not played much in the Premier League so far. If this continues, and Arsenal sign another forward, it could cause an issue.

For now, though, there is little evidence that Gyökeres is trying to leave the club.

He’ll be looking to get regular game time at 28 after finding his scoring touch with Sweden. Arsenal will also need to work out how to use him best as a goalscoring striker.

But for now the January speculation seems a little early. He has stated he wants to stay at Arsenal, and the next few weeks may prove to be more important.

#1971. This West Ham Side Has A Worrying, Dreadfully Familiar Look To It..

With only two points from his first four games, West Ham manager Scott Parker is already coming under pressure, with some even questioning whether he is the right man to take the club forward following last night’s defeat at Portsmouth.

For me, it’s a little premature to be discussing the new manager’s job security. But make no mistake about it, West Ham are a club in crisis, and there is a lot more wrong than just the manager.

However, the one thing Parker can control is how he utilises the players at his disposal. And from my seat in Row B at Fratton Park, it was evident that Parker appears no closer to knowing what his best starting XI is.

Issues in both full-back positions, a lack of creativity through the middle, genuine issues on the left wing and three strikers who can’t score goals.

West Ham huffed and puffed against Pompey, and no doubt the statistics will have been boosted by a late flurry towards the end of the game when we battered the Portsmouth goal for five minutes. But that could not disguise the fact that we were watching a very, very poor West Ham team.

I had a close-up view of West Ham hams problems from row B at Fratton Park

Possibly the most disturbing aspect is that neither Preston North End nor Portsmouth, in our last two games, have looked like particularly good teams. The fact of the matter is that you don’t have to be a decent side to beat West Ham.

We now find ourselves closer to the relegation places than automatic promotion, and I’ve seen little to suggest that anyone knows how to turn us around and get us pointing in the right direction.

There’s a big game coming up at the London Stadium against Stoke City, but make no mistake about it, the Potters will be licking their lips at the prospect of turning over West Ham.

The Hammers are now starting to look less like promotion certainties and more like Leicester City.

#1970. Liverpool's Alexander Isak closes in on Mohamed Salah record with latest Champions League goal

By Matt Law | 25 Nov 2026 21:08, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 21:10

Alexander Isak has now registered in his last six away appearances for Liverpool, with the Sweden international on the scoresheet in Wednesday's Champions League clash with Club Brugge.

The 27-year-old made the breakthrough in the 13th minute of the European fixture, with Liverpool leading 1-0 at the interval.

In the Premier League era, the only player to score in six or more successive away outings for Liverpool is Mohamed Salah, who managed seven between August and October 2021.

Isak is now on nine goals in 16 appearances for Andoni Iraola's side this season, including two in four outings in the Champions League.

#1969. David Raya and Jurrien Timber deals show Arsenal are serious about protecting their title-winning core

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal are continuing their excellent work in retaining their key players as David Raya and Jurrien Timber have both been approached about new contracts.

This comes after Declan Rice signed a five-year contract extension. The midfielder will now stay at the Emirates until 2031, but Mikel Arteta is now close to locking down more defenders in his squad.

Timber has reportedly agreed better terms, and Raya is also on the verge of a new deal. Although both deals are yet to be officially announced, it shows how important Arsenal are trying to keep them at the top.

The importance of retaining Raya and Timber is evident.

Since arriving at the club from Brentford, Raya has become Arteta’s first choice in goal. He has become an important part of Arsenal’s attacking play due to his distribution, decision-making and game under pressure.

His performances have also earned him honours outside of North London as he was named in the 2026 FIFPRO World 11. Only the second Arsenal player to win the award after Thierry Henry in 2006.

Raya has a contract in place until 2028, although he was given better financial terms last year. However, a new long-term deal will offer more security to one of Arteta’s most trusted players.

Since joining from Ajax in 2023, Timber has become a key part of Arsenal’s backline. Despite injury issues, he has proven to be one of the most dependable defenders in the squad.

He can play as a right back, left back and centre back which provides Arteta with great versatility. He has the physicality and technical ability to help Arsenal at both ends of the pitch.

It has been reported that Timber has agreed to better terms. How long his contract is for is unknown.

There is a pattern beginning to emerge from Arsenal’s recent contract news.

Rice has been signed until 2031. Timber is also expected to sign, committing his peak years to the club. Raya is also expected to sign soon, with talks said to be at an advanced stage.

Arteta recently signed a contract extension until 2030. They aren’t just trying to keep their best players for another year but are looking to create consistency within the squad and management.

This is an issue for any club competing within the domestic and European leagues, as it can cause problems with team cohesion and development due to constant change of key players.

While there is still work to be done, this is positive news for fans.

Signing Raya and Timber will ensure that two key components of Arteta’s backline are safe. It will also show that with Rice’s new contract, they’re looking to build on their recent success and not let their best players near the end of their contracts.

It seems AC Milan have made an offer for Endrick in recent days, with a Spanish journalist shocked at the situation.

Talk of Endrick arriving at San Siro is dominating the news, and it’s clear that Milan are not messing around here. Indeed, they are looking to beat off interest from other European clubs and they may well be close to doing so.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Jose Mourinho is still opposing a deal, but the Brazilian’s entourage was in Italy last week and it seems that a move to San Siro is becoming less of a hypothetical and more of a tangible possibility.

Speaking to SER Radio, Anton Meana looked at the reporting from Italy about the Rossoneri’s interest in Endrick and how the situation was actually unfolding.

“AC Milan’s offer is formal and they want to sign him in January. The Rossoneri have already informed the player, and if he can’t leave in January, they’ll see about negotiations in the summer. But AC Milan’s firm offer is now on the table.

“The owner of AC Milan wants to offer close to 70 million euros to sign Endrick now. The problem is that Mourinho prefers to keep him because he knows there wouldn’t be a signing that could match or surpass the Brazilian.

“It’s good for him to have Endrick because he’s good, because he provides competition for Mbappé, and because he trains hard for every match. I want to see how the next few weeks unfold. I’d say Endrick isn’t going to leave, but the player’s entourage, his agents, will be in Madrid this week or early next week seeking talks and exploring the striker’s immediate future.

“I thought it was just the typical bluff from the Italian transfer press, who constantly promote players and see them as being in Serie A all the time, but this offer from Milan, I honestly didn’t expect it. The interest, as Cerruti told you, is very serious, and if they can, they want to sign Endrick this winter transfer window.”

It’s safe to say that the Diavolo’s interest is more than speculative and with an official offer on the table, things may begin to move between Milan and Madrid.

#1967. Talk SPORT reveal comes amidst Scott Parker’s darkest days | West Ham News

There’s talk, behind the scenes, at West Ham regarding the Nuno era that came before and the differences that’ve taken hold under new coach Scott Parker. If anything, on the pitch West Ham have got worse under their former player-turned-head-coach as the slide down the second division continues.

Even with former Hammers legend Mark Noble on the coaching staff, the players look lost and at times without fight or character. Which comes as a shock to supporters who had expected the opposite would be the case with the hugely popular duo at the helm.

As footballers they excelled – but they’re being tested like never before. They still deserve the fans’ support. In my humble opinion. Disagree? Go for it, That’s what we have a ‘comments’ section for.

However, the talk is, apparently, not all doom and gloom.

TalkSPORT’ sAlex Crook, reporting during the Portsmouth v West Ham game, claimed his own exclusive:

“I was speaking to a couple of West Ham staff and they were saying, even if the results aren’t coming, the general atmosphere is a lot better than it was under Nuno.”

If that is the case and there’s progress off the pitch then we as fans will just have to suck it up and get behind this group. They’re the only 26 available until January and whilst they aren’t very good, the majority are at least, trying.

Noble and Parker have to pick the eleven who will try their hearts out and run over hot coals for their manager and their supporters.

At least then the players won’t hang back for fear of being abused amidst away-end ‘ugly scenes‘ after the final whistle as the BBC reported.

That surely has to stop, however frustrated supporters feel. It won’t make the players perform any better. The opposite, in fact.

#1966. Arsenal’s Piero Hincapié contract plans show how quickly his importance has grown

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal are said to be trying to reward Piero Hincapié with better contract terms after just months since making his move permanent.

According to reports, negotiations are at an advanced stage between the Ecuadorian and international players. David Raya is also near to signing a new contract as Mikel Arteta looks to retain his key squad members.

However, Hincapié is in a slightly different position compared to his teammates. The 24-year-old only signed a five-year deal permanently in the summer.

Therefore, he could be discussing an increase in his salary rather than an extension. It has not been officially confirmed by either Arsenal or the player.

Arsenal have exercised their option to make Hincapié’s loan move from Bayer Leverkusen permanent.

The defender made 39 appearances in all competitions during his first season in North London, scoring one goal and providing two assists. He has become an important part of Arteta’s defensive options.

His versatility has been an asset to Arsenal. His ability to play as a centre-back or left-back meaning he provides another option to utilise when problems occur with injuries or rotation in defence.

However, Hincapié has been overshadowed by Gabriel Magalhães and Riccardo Calafiori, making it a tough battle for playing time.

In the current campaign, he has played just five games in the league, with all of them coming off the bench. A total of 67 minutes has been played.

Hincapié will not be too concerned by this, as Arsenal have plenty of defensive options, and he provides cover in two positions.

The news that Hincapié is in talks is part of a bigger story around the club trying to keep their best players.

Declan Rice has signed a new five-year deal with Jurrien Timber, signing on improved terms. Raya is also said to be close to signing a new deal.

Arteta has already signed his future to the club until 2030. It is clear that they want to keep the continuity going forward after recent success.

While Hincapié has a contract until next year, renegotiating his deal would show how much Arsenal values him.

They may want to reward their players who have quickly become key members of their squad.

He has no reports of being unhappy and looking to leave the club. It seems he is being rewarded for his contributions to the club and to give him security in the long term.

This is a huge vote of confidence for a player who has only just completed his permanent move this summer.

#1965. Arsenal mourns Peter Storey: 1971 Double-winning hero dies aged 81

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal have expressed their condolences in the passing of former player Peter Storey.

Storey was an influential member of one of the most successful sides in the club’s history. The midfielder appeared in 501 games for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, winning the First Division and FA Cup during the 1970/71 season.

Storey was a key figure in the famous run as he helped keep the FA Cup hopes alive with a display against Stoke City.

A statement from the club confirmed his death on Tuesday (17th November). The club will pay tribute to Storey in their Champions League tie against Borussia Dortmund on 24th November.

Storey signed as an apprentice with Arsenal in 1961, and made his first-team debut in October 1965 in a game against Leicester City.

He was later converted to a central midfielder by manager Bertie Mee and coach Don Howe. Storey became an invaluable member of the squad due to his aggressive play, work-rate and versatility.

In 1970 Storey was part of the side that won the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, and the following year Arsenal won the league and FA Cup double.

Storey played a key role in an amazing FA Cup semi-final in April 1971. After Arsenal had looked like they were losing, Storey scored a last-minute penalty to make it 2-2.

Arsenal won the replay to get to the final, beating Liverpool to win their first-ever double.

Storey scored 17 goals in 501 games for Arsenal. This puts him in joint 8th place in the most appearances for the club.

Storey enjoyed success at club level and earned his first cap for England in 1971. He earned a total of 19 caps for England.

He played for England until 1973. In 1977, Storey left Arsenal to join Fulham, meaning he had a 12-year stint at the north London club.

He played 19 games for Fulham before retiring from professional football in 1978.

Following his football career, Storey had a difficult time. He was imprisoned for a number of crimes. In 2010, he wrote an autobiography, True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man, detailing these events in his life.

He will be remembered in Arsenal history for his impressive contribution to the club. Having made 501 appearances for the club, he was a key member of the squad that won the Double in 1971.

Playing against Borussia Dortmund will be a great way for fans to pay tribute to one of the key players in a special time in the history of the club.

#1964. Jude Bellingham backed to become England's greatest ever player amid Premier League 'travesty'

By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 21:20

Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham has been tipped to become England's greatest ever player by former Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Jamie O'Hara, who believes the 23-year-old is already a better footballer than Harry Kane.

Bellingham produced another outstanding Champions League performance on Tuesday, scoring a spectacular goal and providing an assist in Real Madrid's 5-1 victory over PSV Eindhoven at the Bernabeu.

The England international improvised a remarkable volley with the outside of his boot after the ball bounced back towards him on the edge of the penalty area, later describing the strike as the best goal of his career.

His performance prompted an enthusiastic reaction from O'Hara, whose admiration for Bellingham is accompanied by a growing frustration that English football supporters have never had the opportunity to watch him regularly in the Premier League.

Speaking on talkSPORT's The Sports Bar, O'Hara made a bold prediction about Bellingham's international career.

"He's going to be England's greatest ever player. Ever. He's better than Harry Kane, a better player than Kane," the former Tottenham midfielder said.

Coming from a former Spurs player, the comparison carries weight given Kane's achievements for both club and country. England's all-time leading goalscorer has established himself as one of the finest centre-forwards of his generation, although Bellingham's influence on matches comes from a different position.

The Real Madrid midfielder has registered seven goals and five assists in 18 appearances across all competitions this season, with only Kylian Mbappe directly contributing to more goals for Los Blancos in La Liga.

His ability to influence proceedings from midfield while regularly producing decisive contributions in the final third makes him a valuable player for England. By the time Euro 2028 comes around, Bellingham should be approaching the peak years of his career, with considerable experience of European football already behind him.

O'Hara also described it as a "travesty" that Premier League supporters do not get to watch the midfielder in domestic action every week. However, fellow pundit Jason Cundy suggested that Bellingham's decision to develop his career outside England may have contributed to his success.

Unlike many of England's leading internationals, Bellingham has built his reputation almost entirely outside his homeland. He left Birmingham City for Borussia Dortmund in 2020 at the age of 17 before joining Real Madrid three years later.

His time in Germany allowed him to establish himself as a regular at Champions League level while still a teenager. At Madrid, he won both La Liga and the Champions League in his debut campaign, scoring 23 goals across all competitions.

The prospect of Bellingham eventually playing in the Premier League appears increasingly distant, with Real Madrid reportedly in advanced negotiations over a new long-term contract.

According to The Athletic, the Spanish giants intend to announce an agreement before the end of the calendar year, with Bellingham expected to receive a significant increase on his current annual salary of approximately £12.6m.

His existing deal already runs until June 2029, meaning Real Madrid are under little immediate pressure to negotiate. Their willingness to offer improved terms more than two and a half years before its expiry reflects the importance they attach to retaining the midfielder.

For England, there is little sporting reason to regret Bellingham's absence from the Premier League. He is developing at one of Europe's most demanding clubs and gaining experience in the latter stages of major competitions. The disappointment expressed by O'Hara is understandable from a spectator's perspective, but the Three Lions may benefit from the unconventional route their midfielder has taken.

#1961. Arsenal handed potential midfield advantage as Newcastle face Joelinton injury setback

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal head to St James’ Park this Saturday for their first match after the international break. They could be faced with a weakened Newcastle midfield.

Joelinton missed training before the international break because of a thigh injury that also kept him out of the 1-1 draw with Fulham. Now, he needs to have an MRI scan to check the seriousness of his injury.

This is a huge blow for Jaissle. Joelinton’s physicality and intensity will be very difficult to find in another player, especially when the Gunners put pressure on Newcastle.

It may help Mikel Arteta’s team to dominate in midfield. They must ensure that they match the level of physicality of Newcastle and adjust with the away game itself. Joelinton’s absence may require Newcastle to make some changes in their style of play from midfield.

Joelinton has struggled to make an impact in the Premier League this season. He’s played only three games, and is now set to be sidelined again.

However, it has been suggested that Joelinton could return before Christmas. Further medical tests must be performed to determine the exact amount of time that he will be out for.

Joelinton is a concern. He is very physical and can regain the ball effectively in midfield. He can also help Newcastle move the ball forward.

If Newcastle are unable to match that intensity, it could allow Arsenal to dominate the game. Declan Rice and Bruno Guimarães are both in good form, meaning that the Gunners have a solid foundation in order to succeed, and stop the hosts from taking control.

Willock and Gonzalez have both been absent due to illness, but they should be fit to play on Saturday.

Jaissle has more options to consider with Joelinton missing. Jacob Ramsey is also now available after serving his suspension.

Newcastle have some good news regarding Matias Fernandez-Pardo. The £51 million signing has been suffering from a long-term virus and was unable to play in Belgium’s last internationals. However, he appears to be improving.

He has returned to training so could make the starting XI after coming on as a substitute in the game against Fulham. Since moving to the club from France, he has played 6 games in the Premier League.

Despite Joelinton being absent, Newcastle will still be a dangerous opponent. A calm performance from Arsenal will be required in order to take 3 points from the match.

With Joelinton missing, Arsenal can assert control in midfield. As they look to stay on top of the league table, exploiting the injury issues in Newcastle’s team should be a priority.

#1959. AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone: Five things we learned – centrality and consistency

AC Milan put on a show at San Siro on Sunday night as they swept Frosinone aside emphatically, beating them 5-1.

The own-goal that Gabriele Calvani scored a few minutes in set the tone for the visitors, while Goncalo Ramos broke his drought after starting and finishing a counter-attack. However, Patrizio Masini’s goal shortly after meant the deficit was halved going into the break.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the second half, Milan ran riot. Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse both had opportunities after being found in behind, and both just minutes after coming off the bench. Then, Christian Pulisic added the finishing touch to make it a five-star night.

It was a win that Milan needed, considering that only Inter out of the current top six, dropped points, and it moves the Rossoneri back into the top four spots. Ivan Stoev has picked out the key talking points from the game.

Technically, Rabiot won the MOTM in our post-game ratings, but we absolutely have to talk about Luka Modric.

I’ve personally had my doubts about the Croatian being able to keep up this season, especially under Ruben Amorim. We all expected the Portuguese coach to bring a lot of intensity to Milan’s game and at times, Modric has seemed to struggle.

Maybe that was because of the team adapting to the new coach, or maybe the midfielder hadn’t completely recovered after the World Cup – who knows.

The reality is that the former Real Madrid man has stepped up after some shaky games at the start of the season and continues to prove his quality on and off the ball and his athleticism and longevity are nothing short of extraordinary.

The vision and passing ability to play the through ball to Rabiot for the opening goal was world-class. He then continued to dictate the tempo and make impressive forward runs, playing the full 90 minutes, giving it his all until the final whistle.

The management really needs to assemble a whole group of people tasked to find a proper replacement for Modric, as he will leave a big gap in that midfield.

To continue with the midfielder theme, we also have to give praise to Rabiot, who has been absolutely brilliant this season. Don’t get me wrong, he was one of the Rossoneri’s best players last year too.

Yet he has found a higher level since the start of the campaign, as he racked up another two assists and forced the own goal. As a result, he now has five goals and seven assists in 10 games in Serie A – extraordinary numbers.

On top of the goal contributions, you can count on the Frenchman to be composed under pressure, tidy with his passing, and efficient in both phases of the game. An absolutely stunning start of the season for Rabiot, who is finding new levels to his game under Amorim.

It was such a dominant win that we can probably cover each player and the positives from their game. Nevertheless, one man needs to be praised for sure and that’s Goncalo Ramos, who got himself back on the scoresheet.

Needless to say, he opened up a lot of spaces for his teammates and had a role in some of the other goals, which he was doing even when he failed to get the ball in the back of the net. This time around, he also got his long-awaited goal.

It was a beauty too, in the sense that he dropped deep into his own half, made the tackle to win the ball and kicked off the counter-attack. Following that, he made the run into the opponent’s box and finished it calmly – it was beautifully orchestrated with Ramos in the centre.

The goal and the encouraging performance are also a relief, as we’ve seen many times how strikers struggle to react when they are not scoring, with the confidence level often dropping which results in overall poor form.

However, the Portuguese striker is clearly not in his head and reacted well to a poor spell that spanned both his club and the national team, as he struggled in the international break too.

We didn’t even see that much of him as Amorim subbed him off rather early and it probably has to do with the fact that Milan need a win on Thursday against Olympiacos, in Greece, and Ramos will most likely start the game as the margin for error is little as things stand.

I mean, what more can you ask from your attackers? Diego Moreira got the hockey assist on the second goal and got an assist for Cisse in the second half and on top of that, was heavily involved and dangerous when the Diavolo went on the counter.

Truthfully, the Belgian should have probably scored a goal or two as he had some very good chances in the opponent’s penalty box, but his shooting let him down this time around. Nevertheless, another electric performance.

Speaking of electric – Pulisic also did very well as he was involved in the first goal – even if it ended up being an own goal, his run forced the Frosinone defender to run back and eventually put the ball in his own net.

The American then got his goal in the second half with a composed finish. He had a very solid game overall with lots of smart movements and combination play- nothing flashy, but the efficiency was there.

Then we also have Cisse, who started the game on the bench but only needed nine or so minutes after coming on to get his goal. Ridiculously, he now has six in 10 in the league or a goal every 74 minutes. The youngster made a good run and managed to keep himself onside in a tricky situation and then finished with composure.

The variety in attack by Milan on the night was a joy to watch, as all the players posed a threat to Frosinone, which in the end was too much for them to handle.

Amorim was well aware of how Frosinone would approach the game, which in itself deserves credit as they came to San Siro to play football instead of sitting back. Unfortunately for them and fortunately for us, the coach and his players knew exactly how to get around the high press.

The Rossoneri were rapid on the counter and created so many chances that the score could’ve easily been even worse for Frosinone. Their high press also didn’t work, as for the majority of the game the Diavolo managed to move the ball around quickly enough, which prevented their opponents from winning it in dangerous areas.

It also must be said that the Portuguese did well to rest some key players after the third goal, as he will need a fresh lineup for the Europa League fixture on Thursday, where Milan need three points against Olympiacos.

#1957. TV cash payout for each of the 20 Premier League clubs revealed by new annual EPL 2025-26 report

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

It has now been revealed what each of the 20 Premier League clubs received from the 2025-26 TV cash payouts.

The information made public via the publication of the EPL’s official 2025-26 annual report.

This report including a breakdown of how much money each of last season’s 20 Premier League clubs banked.

In total, the 20 Premier League clubs received £3,142m for the 2025-26 season.

This is a 10.9% increase on the 2024-25 season.

Banking the most were Arsenal with £198.1m, whilst Wolves received the least with £117.2m.

The Premier League is actually one of the very fairest major European leagues in terms of the gap between which clubs get the very most and very least. Arsenal getting 1.69 x what Wolves received.

This is the breakdown of the total distributions of £3,142m between the 20 Premier League clubs (in order of placings in the Premier League table for the 2025-26 season):

£198.1m Arsenal £192.7m Man City £191.3m Man U £182.1m Aston Villa £181.6m Liverpool £170.2m Bournemouth £167.7m Sunderland £161.7m Brighton £160.8m Brentford £163.4m Chelsea £154.5m Fulham £153.7m Newcastle United £147.1m Everton £144.2m Leeds £136.4m Palace £135.9 Forest £136.6m Spurs £127.9m West Ham £118.6m Burnley £117.2m Wolves

As you can see, some clubs got more than one or more of those that finished above them in the table. This is due to how many times the relative clubs were chosen for live UK coverage, this is the ‘Facility Fees’ portion of the cash.

The Newcastle United total of £153.7m is broken down as:

UNITED KINGDOM (VIA THE TV DEALS ETC.) Equal Share £31.9m Facility Fees £20.3m Merit £15.4m

OVERSEAS (VIA THE TV DEALS ETC.) Equal Share £56.5m Merit £18.4m

Newcastle United received £6.5m less than 2024-25 as they fell eight places in the Premier League table. However, it would have been a far bigger drop without the overall 10.9% increase in the entire share out and the fact that NUFC were selected 31 times for UK TV coverage across 2025-26.

Bruno Fernandes scored a bizarre long-range effort in Manchester United's Champions League contest with Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday night.

The 20-time English champions trailed at the interval of the European fixture, with Luis Suarez scoring from the penalty spot after a rash challenge from Senne Lammens.

Suarez had missed a first-half penalty following a tackle from Lisandro Martinez but was able to register at the second time of asking to send the Portuguese outfit ahead.

However, the match turned in the early stages of the second period, with Fernandes first scoring from the penalty spot to level it at 1-1 before netting a second two minutes later.

There did not appear to be much danger for Sporting when Fernandes sent an attempt towards the home side's goal, but it took an incredible bounce off the turf before flying past goalkeeper Kaique Pereira, who could not believe what had happened.

#1955. Christos Tzolis challenges Arsenal critics with a message about his physicality

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Winger Christos Tzolis wants to prove he has a lot to offer Arsenal beyond his attacking prowess.

Since moving to the club from Club Brugge in July, the 24-year-old has made a great start to life at the club after an impressive season in Belgium. The Greek attacker scored 17 goals and made 23 assists in 36 league games.

But doubts were raised about his ease of integration into the Premier League. In his first stint in England with Norwich City, he showed little sign of becoming the player he is now.

Since making his debut for the club, Tzolis has become a more rounded attacking threat. He has started all 7 Premier League games this season and provides a reliable option on the left for Arteta.

However, in recent comments, it seems that he is aware of the perceptions around his physicality and is keen to change them.

Tzolis spoke to Arsenal Media, saying that he doesn’t think the notion of him lacking the physicality to play at top level has validity.

He claimed that he is not a player without muscle and cited his accomplishments. He also described his tendency to use aggression against his opponents.

This is a key part of Arteta’s system at the club. Tzolis is expected to press from the flanks if Arsenal lose the ball.

Tzolis is comfortable with this role. He is able to track back well to support his full-back, adding an extra dimension to the left side.

The Greek international has proven his physical ability outside of match play. He was nicknamed Leonidas by the fitness team at the club due to a strong performance in pre-season.

It is reported that he completed the running challenge better than anyone in the squad.

Tzolis has joined Arsenal to add attacking flair to the squad, having left for Besiktas. He looks like he could be a formidable goalscorer and creator.

In the league last season, Tzolis contributed 40 goals and put in a good performance in Europe. This led to Arsenal spending a reported £34 million to bring him to the club.

He has not had the best impact in the league, registering just one assist and no goals, but this should not be taken to mean he is not contributing.

Tzolis has shown an ability to fit into Arteta’s style of play. His defensive contribution, work rate and combative nature may prove very valuable in tough away games.

Despite there being plenty to improve on, Tzolis provides more than just an attacking option for Arsenal.

If Tzolis can change people’s view of him in terms of his physicality and continues to put his technical skills and determination together, then he can be a valuable asset in Arteta’s plans.

#1953. Double boost for Matthias Jaissle on Newcastle United injury and fitness front

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Matthias Jaissle hadn’t had the best of luck when it comes to injuries with his Newcastle United squad.

However, for the Arsenal match last weekend it looked like the treatment/recovery room was almost cleared.

Ewen Jaouen and Joelinton appearing to be the only senior players unable to be considered for the match against the league leaders, with Matthias Jaissle appearing to omit Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure purely  by choice, with others favoured.

So after getting to that point of all but clearing the treatment room out and on the back of such a positive second half performance and excellent result against Arsenal, the last thing the United boss needed was to see any new injuries.

Just as an absorbing Arsenal game had gone into the nine minutes of added time, Lewis Hall was left limping after he had blocked a cross and tried to carry on, was then having to limp off a minute or so later and be replaced by Sven Botman.

Following the match, Matthias Jaissle asked whether Lewis Hall was now an injury worry: “Hopefully it is only just a cramp that meant Lewis Hall had to come off. That is what we are hoping.”

Newcastle United have now posted clips from the training ground ahead of the Brighton match and the great news is that they show Lewis Hall sprinting out with the rest of the first team squad for group training, clearly no lasting impact from Saturday and Jaissle’s cramp diagnosis/hope proved correct.

There is also other good news on the injury and fitness front.

It was feared that Joelinton would be out for a considerable time when suffering a muscle injury during the home defeat to Everton in early November.

However, a new media exclusive from The Mail has now reported that their inside sources have informed them that the prognosis isn’t as bad as had first been feared and that Joelinton is now expected to resume full training next week, ahead of the Man U and Sunderland matches at St James’ Park.

You would assume Man U is almost certainly too early but if he doesn’t have any setbacks, it sounds very much like a chance the Brazil international could potentially feature against the mackems.

Not that there were any fears raised about him after the weekend but it’s still great to see Tino Livramento heavily involved in the training footage released by the club on Wednesday.

He reminded us against Arsenal just how good he can be and a huge boost for everyone if he can now stay fit and be in the kind of form he showed on Saturday.

Matthias Jaissle was asked about the right-back after the Arsenal match: “Tino can definitely give us another dimension to our play but we also have to be careful and smart. He was really on the limit of what he could do. I was really proud that he could deliver 45 minutes with that physicality in such an intense match. It was really well played, a top performance, and also something that he can build on.”

A huge eight days of matches coming up and Matthias Jaissle needs as many of his key players as possible available, as United take on Brighton, Man U and Sunderland.

#1952. All of the frustration, none of the magic | West Ham’s latest enigma

Watching last night’s woeful performance against Portsmouth unfold, I was struck by the similarity in playing style of one current West Ham winger with a previous playing enigma from whom West Ham could never seem to coax the best.

Triggered by the  irritation generated from watching Manor Solomon constantly check back, slow down play and then inevitably cut inside, I found myself comparing him with another West Ham winger who repeated the same trick ad nauseam.

Even on the one occasion when he was put clean through beyond his full back, by a brilliant pass from Ezra Mayers, Solomon got to the by line and – infuriatingly, checked back instead of trying to cross with his weaker foot.

And at that moment I thought “Saïd Benrahma” all over again.

The enigma that was Saîd Benrahma: at least he scored a few, created a few, and smacked a mean penalty past Fiorentina’s keeper in the summer of 2023.

‘Benny’ could at least create chances (and score a mean penalty) whereas Manor Solomon just runs down blind alleys, head down, inevitably slowing and cutting inside to use his right foot.

Exactly as, on numerous occasions in each game, the Algerian would check back, infuriatingly, and slow up play instead of pressing on to beat his full back on the inside or out. In that respect Solomon seems identical, disrupting West Ham’s flow, allowing defenders to reset and frustrating the bejesus out of supporters.

At least Benrahma could create and occasionally score: Solomon has, by the reckoning of westhamworld.co.uk, now played “1141 minutes for two goals and two assists, averaging a goal every 285 minutes”.

For whatever reason the Israeli clearly is a shadow of the player who helped fire Leeds to promotion and West Ham need to consign him to the same ‘rest and recuperation’ home in which Mads Hermansen has been sent to recapture his form.

Austbo at least has a shot on him and seems to be able to beat players inside and out: With the Norwegian there is the feeling that there’s more to come. With Solomon, exactly as Tottenham fans suggested, the fear is that his best days are long in the rear view mirror. Much like Saîd Benrahma, but without the trophy to show for it.

#1950. Arsenal transfer dilemma: Alex Scott and Nico Paz could force difficult decisions for Arteta

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Potential signings of Alex Scott and Nico Paz may pose a challenge for Arteta.

While both players would add quality to the squad, their arrival would be a consideration for current players in the Emirates squad.

Scott would add quality in midfield, and Paz adds creativity and versatility going forward. Arteta must consider that adding these players may hinder the development of current players.

Arsenal are believed to be keen on bringing Alex Scott to the club.

After rejecting contract offers from Bournemouth, Scott could only have one year left on his contract at the club next summer. However, he is understood to be valued by Bournemouth at over £100m.

He would be a great addition for Arteta, with the versatility and skill he has. He could give added competition in midfield.

Yet his potential arrival raises questions about Myles Lewis-Skelly’s future role.

Myles Lewis-Skelly was included in the Champions League final line-up last season. He showed that he is trusted by the club.He has also demonstrated his commitment by remaining at the club despite opportunities to gain regular playing time at other clubs.

Signing another expensive midfielder may present difficulties. It is unclear at this point whether Scott will be a useful addition to the squad or simply overcrowd this area of the team.

Nico Paz presents another interesting option for Arsenal.

Paz joined Como from Real Madrid in the summer. He has caught the eye of a number of big clubs and has increased his appeal with strong performances in international football. The 22-year-old has scored 5 times in his last 5 games for Argentina.

Paz is a versatile right-sided player and could be an appealing addition to Arteta’s strike force.

There are already plenty of players fighting for attacking positions at Arsenal.

Bukayo Saka is key in the team’s attack, and with Martin Ødegaard and Noni Madueke in the squad too, there are plenty of options. Max Dowman is a young player looking to break into the first team.

While Paz would add quality to the squad, Arsenal would need to find a specific role for him. There are complications with the move, though. Real Madrid have an option to re-sign him in 2027 for 80 million euros.

Although Arsenal are facing challenges in attracting quality players to the club. They now also face issues in managing a squad with experienced internationals and developing young players.

Although Scott and Paz would improve the depth of the squad, players must not be sacrificed for new players if they have already shown quality.

Players such as Lewis-Skelly and Dowman may be negatively affected by this. Opportunities may be taken away from them if the club continues to spend large amounts of money on new players.

However, it is still very important for Arsenal to bring in quality players to compete for major titles.

Know how the additions will integrate within the playing style and how they affect the other players within the squad.

The Gunners can strengthen further without overloading the squad. Good additions can be made to the first XI whilst also providing a realistic chance for young players to come through from within the academy.

#1949. ‘Manchester United break the bank for Newcastle United’s Lewis Hall’ Mikael Silvestre

Mikael Silvestre has been talking about Manchester United and Lewis Hall.

The former Manchester United left-back (and central defender) speaking ahead of the next transfer window.

Just over five weeks now until that January 2027 window opens.

The Manchester United defence continuing to be a total shambles and Mikael Silvestre discussing players that the media have speculated as being of interest to Man U.

The four names put to Mikael Silvestre are Chelsea’s Malo Gusto, Fulham’s Antonee Robinson and Calvin Bassey, as well as Newcastle United’s Lewis Hall.

The former Man U defender making clear to BestBettingBonuses what he thinks about the Chelsea player: “Manchester United should definitely not be looking to sign Malo Gusto…I think it would be crazy to bring in a player like Gusto into a United defence that is so unsettled. You don’t want to add more problems.”

Mikael Silvestre then considering the Fulham pair: “I have to be honest, neither Robinson or Bassey are players that excite me or who I think would upgrade the Man U defence. Manchester United need to sign players that are going to raise the level, and those players wouldn’t do that.”

Mikael Silvestre: “Lewis Hall? That is different. I think he is the type of player that would absolutely raise the level and add value to the squad. He signed a new contract, so that means that Newcastle will command a bigger fee for him, but it doesn’t mean he isn’t available. If he is the player that Manchester United have identified to add quality to the defence, then you have to go and be ambitious and break the bank to get him. It would be a huge fee, but it would also secure the future of the left back position for the next decade because Hall is a young guy. I only want to see Man U sign players that raise the level. Hall would be one of them. It’s not a luxury signing, I think it’s an essential piece of business if he is the guy that you want to get.”

Mikael Silvestre of course missing the most important factor.

If Lewis Hall did ever decide to leave Newcastle United, why on earth would he choose Manchester United?

The lifelong United fan would have his pick of numerous successful clubs, so why join the shambles at Old Trafford?

#1948. Alarming parallels should be heeded as Hammers hit the bottom half of the table | West Ham News

Sure it couldn’t happen, could it? Only five times in the history of the Premier League have sides suffered successive relegations from the top tier to the third.

For anyone who witnessed the shambolic showing at Fratton Park on Tuesday night, that nightmare scenario suddenly doesn’t look so  ridiculous. West Ham in the third division, 62,500 seater stadium and all?

Alarming parallels exist between West Ham’s performance this season and that of their former competitors Leicester City who now find themselves playing their football in the third division.

The Hammers are now in the bottom half of the Championship, with just 24 points from 17 games. At the same stage last season, the Foxes themselves, after 17 games had amassed … Exactly the same number of points.

All of which seemed unimaginable when the Irons beat Swansea five weeks ago to go second, and Nuno Espirito Santo picked upthe September manager of the month award.

Fratton Park showing was a real wake up call to West Ham’s management and board. This ship is sinking.

The only positive is that a month is a long time in this league. A run of form could be just around the corner and any team – West Ham included – can win five or six games and transform their fortunes. But the Hammers’ form at present is most definitely that of a relegation candidate rather than a play-off hopeful.

Which hardly helps the recruitment in January.

For anyone living under the misconception that Leicester City’s case was an isolated example and that lightning couldn’t strike twice, Wolverhampton Wanderers, who were also relegated in 2012/13, had 22 points after 17 games.

Stoke City come calling on Saturday with a seriously impressive run of form, unbeaten in six whereas the Hammers are winless in their last half dozen. No time like the present to get back to winning ways and arrest the downhill slide. One relegation is enough, thank you very much.

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

We don’t have a keeper who inspires confidence and we don’t have a striker who looks like scoring goals. In between the two we play more side to side than front to back.

The incompetent ways in which the club has been run are really biting now.

We look a million miles away from a promotion winning team. The Preston and Portsmouth results were dire.

Leicester City had a points deduction last season.

#1946. Max Dowman’s Arsenal return: Is the teenage star one to watch, and can he keep his nose clean?

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Max Dowman shortly returns to action for Arsenal after serving a three-game suspension.

His absence has been disappointing, but the experience should give the youngster an important lesson. Can he put the incident behind him and show Mikel Arteta that he can be trusted?

Dowman received a red card against Fleetwood Town after kicking out at Harrison Neal. Arsenal appealed the decision, but the FA rejected the club’s appeal.

The suspension ruled him out of three domestic fixtures against Liverpool, Hull City and Newcastle United.

He’ll be back on 29 November as Arsenal take on Manchester City. This should give the young star a chance to get his season back on track and showcase what makes him such a highly-rated player.

Dowman looks very promising for the future. He has shown great adaptability playing with the more experienced players and has the self-belief to make an impact in games.

He has performed well in the Carabao Cup. In the 4-2 win against Ipswich, Dowman scored two goals, showing his flair and poise in front of goal.

Arteta has given him opportunities to play in the Premier League and Champions League, meaning that he appears to have a clear route into the first team.

Although Dowman still has a lot to learn, he displays great potential in his technical ability and combative nature. As he gets more games under his belt, fans will be excited to see how he progresses.

Dowman was sent off in an unfortunate moment. He was heavily challenged by Neal and, after lashing out, was shown a straight red card.

Although this one moment should not be enough to dismiss a young player from the game completely, it can serve as a valuable lesson on the pressure that comes with playing at a higher level.

Opponents will test Dowman physically, but he must learn to keep his composure. As he starts making an impact, some players may target his age and inexperience to unsettle him.

As he gets more game time, consistency will be key. Arteta must be confident that Dowman can be relied on in high pressure situations.

Arsenal do not need to rush Dowman into the first team. The squad’s quality allows Arteta to manage his minutes and give him time to develop without putting too much pressure on him.

If Dowman is to play against Manchester City, it will depend on Arteta’s plans, but he has certainly done enough to warrant consideration.

The suspension should not define his season. What matters now is how he responds, both on and off the pitch.

Dowman has the talent to become an important player for Arsenal. Keeping his discipline will be just as important as displaying his ability.

#1945. “Staring Parker in the Face” West Ham’s Missing Link Hiding In Plain Sight

I wrote yesterday that I was struggling for answers regarding how West Ham can address their current form. And then, like a lightning bolt, it all became a lot clearer to me!

Some players influence matches in ways that do not always show up in the highlights package. And West Ham have two such players, one of whom has been overlooked by Scott Parker.

The player overlooked is none other than Pablo Felipe.

Now, before we get ahead of ourselves, I’ve openly never been a big fan of the player. He barely scores any goals, looks slow and has missed some great opportunities in front of goal.

However, while Pablo Felipe may not always grab the headlines, the numbers indicate he is one of the most influential players in our squad.

When Pablo starts, West Ham score first in 83.6% of matches. Without him in the starting line-up, that figure plummets to just 18.2%. In football, scoring first can completely change the course of a game, making this a significant indicator of his influence.

The defensive numbers are equally striking. With Pablo on the pitch, the team have scored 16 goals while conceding only five. Without him, they have scored 19 but conceded 19. While the attacking output remains similar, the defensive stability and overall balance are clearly stronger when he plays.

“Staring Parker in the Face” West Ham’s Missing Link? The gaffer could do worse than select Pablo

This highlights something many supporters already recognise. Pablo’s value lies in his work rate, intelligent positioning, pressing and ability to knit the team together. He helps the side control matches, protects the defence and creates the conditions for others to shine.

With few options and players underperforming, Parker may look to reintegrate the Portuguese striker into the first-team set-up for the visit of Stoke City on Saturday.

The other player who deserves a place in the starting eleven is Tomáš Souček. Despite featuring for just 182 minutes across nine matches, he has already registered three goals and eleven shots. With the team in desperate need of leaders, Souček’s influence could prove invaluable. Fiercely respected within the dressing room, the midfielder has earned the nickname “Iron Man” from his teammates and it’s easy to see why! As Kris has already reported, this hasn’t gone unnoticed elsewhere!

Former manager David Moyes once summed up his importance perfectly: “We rely on him a lot, we need him, and he is very important for us.”

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

#1943. Arsenal transfer news: Why Kevin Schade could be a smart January signing

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal are looking to strengthen their attacking options in January. One player they are reportedly keeping an eye on is Brentford winger Kevin Schade. Mikel Arteta will be keen to add competition in attack, and Schade may be a good option.

Schade will give additional pace to the offence. He is capable of playing in multiple attacking positions to provide Arteta with extra depth in the squad.

However, it may be difficult to get Schade. He is on loan at Brentford, and may want to keep him in the long term. If Schade is seen as a key player in the future, they may be difficult to negotiate with.

Schade’s versatility is another big plus. His speed and straightforward method make him hard to deal with for defenders. In addition, he can be used as a left-sided attacker, giving Arteta more flexibility in his front line. As the club are playing in a number of competitions, this can be very useful.

Schade has already scored 3 times in the Premier League this season. He has quickly adapted to playing in England after moving from Freiburg to Brentford in 2023.

Despite only being 24 years old, Schade still has a lot to improve on. He has lots of experience in the Premier League but has not quite reached the peak of his ability yet. If he moves to Arsenal, he may be able to elevate his performance.

Brentford has already started negotiations with Schade regarding a contract extension that would keep him tied to the club for a long time. He is already contracted until the summer of 2028.

Arsenal’s interest could prove problematic. Other clubs are also keeping their eyes on this player. Tottenham in particular are not seen as a major threat at this stage.

It is going to be very challenging for Brentford to let go of Schade because he has played a key part in their offensive setup, and losing Schade could prove disastrous.

Arsenal will have to pay Brentford whatever they ask for, Schade, and since he has a decent amount of time left on his contract, Brentford has an edge in negotiations.

Arsenal’s interest in Schade is logical. His versatility will provide Arteta with additional flexibility because of his prior experience in the Premier League.

It can be considered positive to sign new strikers. Arsenal must decide if they believe that Schade will fit in well with their current players and whether the asking price from Brentford is reasonable.

As of now, there are no signs of a transfer on the horizon, but it is clear that Schade is a player worth monitoring as the winter transfer window approaches.

#1941. Newcastle vs Arsenal: Team news, predicted line-ups and match preview

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal will have a tough task on hand as they visit St James’ Park.

Mikel Arteta’s side are five points clear at the top of the Premier League after their 1-0 victory over Hull City ahead of the international break. The Gunners have now gone nine games unbeaten in all competitions.

Despite only one win in their last six games, Newcastle will be a dangerous side at home.

Although Arsenal have won the last three encounters with Newcastle, recent games at Tyneside have not gone entirely smoothly for Mikel Arteta. He will also have to make a few key decisions in the squad with players injured and a busy run of fixtures.

Bruno Guimaraes will certainly be a topic of discussion for this game. The midfielder joined Newcastle four-and-a-half years ago, playing an important role in the development of the side, before moving to Arsenal on a reported 75 million pound move in the summer.

Whilst he has struggled to make himself an automatic starter in Arteta’s side, he could have a bigger impact with the absence of Martin Zubimendi.

Zubimendi is likely to be out for several weeks. Declan Rice should start, and Guimaraes is also likely to be involved, to form a double pivot.

Newcastle will try to play a gritty game to unsettle Arsenal. Despite Guimaraes’ knowledge of the opposition, he will have to assist the visitors to maintain control of the midfield battle.

Saliba is now back in contention after recovering from a back injury. The Frenchman has not played in the first team this season, but has made two appearances as he recovers. He played 45 minutes for the U21s.

Arteta confirmed that Saliba is in good shape and will begin to play more games, though he is unlikely to be in the starting line-up for the game against Newcastle.

Konsa should be in the starting line-up alongside Gabriel. Saliba could come on from the bench, as he looks to make his first competitive appearance of the season after the Champions League final last time out.

Saka is still unavailable due to quad trouble, whilst Dowman is suspended. Madueke should start on the right and Havertz will spearhead the attack.

Newcastle United: Predicted line-up not confirmed in the supplied team news.

Arsenal: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Guimaraes; Madueke, Odegaard, Tzolis; Havertz.

Arsenal absentees: Martin Zubimendi, Bukayo Saka and Max Dowman.

Saliba is available but is not expected to start.

Newcastle have leaked goals at home this season. However, with Madueke and Tzolis providing pace in wide areas, this should not worry Arsenal too much.

Nevertheless, this game should be challenging for the Gunners. Newcastle are dangerous in attack and can capitalise on errors quickly in possession.

Despite Arsenal’s solid defensive record, they have failed to keep a clean sheet in their 4 visits to St James’ Park.

Overall this should be a good watch with goals scored by both sides. However, Arsenal should be able to pick up some vital 3 points.

Predicted score: Newcastle United 2-3 Arsenal.

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has bemoaned the decisions that went against his side in Wednesday's 2-2 draw with Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League.

An incredible match saw three penalties awarded, while Man United had two goals controversially disallowed, one in each half of the European fixture.

Luis Suarez missed his first penalty of the night for Sporting before converting his second, while Bruno Fernandes also netted from the spot early in the second half.

The 20-time English champions also had a goal in the first half controversially chalked off, with Youri Tielemans penalised for what looked to be a fair challenge before Amad Diallo converted.

"I was so proud of how my players handled such a tough game. Across the 90 minutes, the personality and character. It's difficult to find in one game where we were so punished," Pochettino told TNT Sports after the contest in Portugal.

"We need to believe more and more. We need to improve things, but that's what we need to show. In the second half we recovered the ball a lot in the opposition's half. That's the way we want to play."

#1939. Křetínský’s Silence Is Becoming A Problem For West Ham

I think we’ve reached a point now where we need some more clarity from West Ham United about the future direction of the football club. Whilst I understand there is an overriding desire to get the Hammers promoted, something which has been described to us by club insiders as a priority, I’m increasingly concerned about how we intend to achieve it.

Because as things stand at the moment, West Ham appear rudderless. In fact, I’d go as far as to say we’re listing. We’re getting progressively worse, and there is a worrying lack of direction at the football club.

Whilst there may be a desire to reach a certain destination, I see very little from West Ham at the moment to suggest that we know the route. And that’s why I believe we really need to hear from Daniel Křetínský.

We’ve waited an awfully long time for the restructuring of West Ham’s shareholding to go through. And whilst Claret & Hugh reported earlier this month that the transactions had been completed, we’re still waiting for public confirmation from the football club.

Křetínský himself has indicated that he will engage with supporters once the share transaction has been finalised, but quite frankly, I don’t think that’s good enough anymore.

West Ham are in desperate need of leadership. Whatever the situation with his shareholding, Křetínský is already in a position of authority at the football club.

West Ham are still waiting for Daniel Kretinsky to address supporters

Whilst I don’t expect him to be shooting from the lip in the way David Sullivan used to, I do think he needs to provide some leadership, some direction and some communication with supporters as to what the actual plan is here.

Because almost everybody at every level of the football club, from the players right up to the very top, appears to be struggling.

Ideally, I’d like to know what the direction of travel is. What is the plan for West Ham United?

They want to take us forward, but how are they going to do that? What’s the plan for January? What’s the plan for investment?

We sold around £200m worth of players during the summer, we’ve yet to see the anticipated injection of funds from the shareholders, and we currently don’t look anything like a team capable of mounting a successful promotion challenge.

And that, by the club’s own admission, is supposed to be the number one priority.

As things stand, the team are getting worse and the club appear to be getting worse. I don’t think West Ham supporters are being unreasonable in wanting to know what the people running our football club intend to do about it.
